body:
> Searches the array in reverse-order for a sub-sequence.

Generally I think this is a good formulation, but `String` refers to 'subsequence' with a different definition (in the function `is_subsequence_of` which is also exposed):
```gdscript
assert("abc".is_subsequence_of("a1b1c1"))
```
I had to look up the term, and I think `String`'s definition for it is correct. Perhaps let's just formulate it like:
```suggestion
				Searches the array in reverse-order for the occurrence of [param sequence].  Optionally, a start search index can be passed. If negative, the start index is considered relative to the end of the array.
```

body: Adjusted wording here, I didn't know "Subsequence" was its own distinct term. Finalized on "Searches ... for an occurrence of the given sequence." which I think reads well.

I know you didn't write the comment, but this would be a good time to fix its spelling:
```suggestion
			return -1; // Won't find anything!
```

I think it would be good to follow along with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104286/ and harmonize boundary logic (explained in my general comment):
```suggestion
			return -1;
```
I think you accidentally swapped types here
The name `find_sequence` would be better than `find_seq`. This is not a super common function so it should not be shortened.

Needs to account for large starting indices:

```suggestion
	if (p_from < 0 || p_from + p_str.length() > length() || p_str.is_empty()) {
```

With this, the next `if` block should be deletable entirely, if I'm not mistaken.
Same for `rfind` implementation (and `vector` versions).

I'm not 100% sure whether `length()` can be optimized out in `String`, since it's in RAM rather than on the stack. It may be better to just keep it in `const int len`, should also reduce your line change count again :)
